# Jubilees Chapter 25 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Rebecca Sends Jacob Away; Her Blessing

---

**25:1** In the second year of the week, Rebecca called Jacob to her and said: "Jacob, my son — do not marry any Canaanite woman, the way your brother Esau has done. He took two wives from among the Canaanites, and they have been nothing but misery to me. Everything they do is impure. Their whole way of life is defined by sexual immorality and lust — there is no righteousness in them at all.

**25:2** I love you more than I can say, my son. My heart overflows for you. And that's why I'm determined to protect you from marrying into that line.

**25:3** Go instead to the home of your grandfather Bethuel and find a wife from your uncle Laban's daughters. Find someone good and upright.

**25:4** I know she'll be right for you. And you'll become a blessing on this earth, and your children after you.

**25:5** I won't count a single day of the rest of my life as a happy day until I see your children — not until I know you've gone to that family and come home with a wife.

**25:6** Go, son. Laban will welcome you with open arms — he'll be thrilled to see you. Choose one of his daughters. I know the LORD will bless you above all my children, because you are the firstborn and the holy one.

**25:7** I'm going to go pray. I'll petition the LORD your God to direct your path and help you find a good wife. And I pray that the LORD will bless all your children with righteousness for every generation to come."

**25:8** Jacob said to Rebecca his mother: "I have no intention of marrying a Canaanite woman — or any woman who isn't right. Your instructions mean the world to me, and so do Abraham's. And father Isaac has told me the same thing: no Canaanite wives.

**25:9** Don't worry about me, mother. I'll do what's right."

**25:10** Rebecca stood up and took Jacob in her arms and kissed him. She loved him more than any of her children.

**25:11** Then she spoke over him: "Be blessed, my son — blessed by the LORD of all things, the God who made heaven and earth. I pray he blesses you above every generation of humans. May he give you righteousness and holiness. May he make you holy. May he plant your feet on the earth, establish you, and lift you up.

**25:12** I am going to go and bless the LORD your God and pray for you. May you walk the right path. May you be blessed with blessings from heaven above and earth below, from the light above and the depths beneath.

**25:13** May your children fill the earth from east to west, from north to south. May all the angels of the presence bless you and march ahead of you.

**25:14** Hold your ground, my son. Fear no one. Don't lose heart. You will reign over all the descendants of Seth.

**25:15** You — you and your line alone — have been chosen to rule over all the earth. Among every nation and every people, you will be great in the LORD's name. They will call you servants of the Most High. You will be the children and heirs of the living God of heaven.

**25:16** Every spirit of truth is on your side. Every angel of light is with you, and they rejoice in the LORD. You will have dominion over his sanctuary, and no impurity will be found there.

**25:17** So go, my son. May the LORD God be with you. Let me live long enough to see your children and hear good news about them before I go to join my ancestors."

**25:18** Jacob said, "I am truly blessed, mother, and I will be. I will follow every one of the LORD's commandments, and my ways will be righteous. I will never forget you — I will seek the LORD every day of my life.

**25:19** I bless you in return. Blessed are you, and blessed is everything you've ever done. You've loved me and looked out for me, and I'm deeply grateful for your blessing."

**25:20** Afterward, Rebecca called Esau to her and said: "Please, son — don't marry a Canaanite woman."

**25:21** Esau answered her: "I won't. I'll take a wife from the daughters of Ishmael — from grandfather's line." Rebecca felt relieved.

**25:22** Then Isaac called Jacob and blessed him and told him: "Don't take a wife from among the Canaanites. Go — travel to Mesopotamia, to the house of your grandfather Bethuel, and marry one of Laban's daughters, your mother's brother.

**25:23** May God Almighty bless you and make you grow into a great multitude — a whole community of nations. May he give you the blessing he gave Abraham — to you and to your children after you — so that you will inherit the land where your ancestors lived as strangers, all the land God gave to Abraham."

---
*PNEUMA notes: Rebecca's blessing (vv.11-16) is the emotional heart of the chapter — more elaborate than anything in Genesis. The dual commission (Rebecca's in vv.1-7, Isaac's in vv.22-23) frames Jacob's departure to Laban. "All the seed of Seth" (v.14) = all humanity; the phrase echoes Balaam's oracle (Num 24:17).*
